record.file_problem: Repository README and file listing only; code and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports outcomes of English-derived weight edits on refusal, including across languages and model checkpoints. This tests practical removal and transfer using a weight edit rather than the original activation ablation/addition method.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal outcomes and weight-edit comparisons. It also mentions many selection-objective, geometry, and planned-experiment results; those are not rows unless they measure refusal or a claim-version outcome. Planned experiments and values used only to motivate later tests are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The study applies Heretic abliteration, a difference-in-means refusal-direction weight edit, to Gemma-3-12B-it and its Slovene sibling GaMS3-12B-Instruct. It reports judged refusal before and after the edit in English and Slovene. This tests V2 (does the weight edit remove refusal?) and V6 (does an English-derived edit carry to Slovene?) in a new cross-lingual setting. The extensive placement experiments show the removal depends on which layers are edited.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The headline surviving finding is that WHERE in depth the English-derived edit sits decides how much refusal survives. A mid-depth band (about layers 13-24) removes it; a late band at the same energy or double the dose does not. This holds in Gemma, in GaMS3 and in Qwen3-8B, and the band is shared across languages and siblings; the authors explicitly falsify language- and checkpoint-specific readings. The authors add two further results. Heretic's English keyword objective is structurally blind in Slovene. The residual EN/SL asymmetry under a well-placed edit concerns actionability, not refusal. The GaMS3 87% to 0% versus Gemma 94% to 74% contrast is attributed to a badly placed, under-dosed selected edit, not to the models.
record.recipe_differences: The reported intervention is a Heretic-family English-derived weight edit, evaluated for refusal outcomes and edit placement. The original claim's difference-in-means activation direction ablation/addition is not reported. Repository kind: experiment/research artifact collection.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports outcome differences by model, language, edit placement, and matched removal energy/layer count. Gemma strict refusal differs by language under the best-placed edit; broad refusal is reported equal across English and Slovene.

fits_no_version.finding: After the edit, Slovene non-refusals are more often guard-safe (non-actionable) than English ones (0.338 vs 0.106). Rubric ASR is 0.93 EN versus 0.72 SL under the best-placed edit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After abliteration, the actionability of compliant outputs can differ by language even when refusal rates converge.

fits_no_version.finding: Heretic's English keyword refusal counter scores 0% on Slovene responses that a judge rates 82% refusals. Its floor sits above the selection threshold, so it mis-selects candidate edits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: English keyword-based refusal metrics used to tune abliteration fail to detect refusal in other languages.

record.problems: The README says Slovene is machine-translated and native-speaker review is pending. It also reports judge-agreement concerns for Slovene in earlier evaluations. The README and file list were available, but the underlying code and result files were not inspected or run. No general-capability preservation result is reported for the weight edits.
record.rows_left_out: The README contains many other results on objective mis-scoring, direction geometry, calibration, and planned final-round experiments. They were omitted because they do not directly report the refusal outcome or another measure named by the claim versions; proposed experiments are not results. Also omitted are further matched-band rank summaries and intermediate objective values that do not add a separate model-by-condition refusal outcome.

untested.parts: No activation-level ablation or addition of the direction, no induction of refusal, and no general-capability check reported in the README.
Preservation of general capabilities after the edit: exp5 utility results are referenced but not given in the README.
Transfer from base to instruct models, and transfer of a direction across checkpoints. The cross-checkpoint result concerns band placement profiles, not a transferred direction.
Not tested; the authors state no attribution to any training stage.

missing.what: Extreme placement contrast in Gemma: layers 16-31 give EN 0.07 / SL 0.27, while layers 33-48 at the same energy give EN 0.92 / SL 0.92. A 2x dose of the late-band edit still leaves EN 0.88 / SL 0.92.
Gemma post-edit judged refusal of 13% English versus 82% Slovene (Delta_lang -1.56 [-1.68, -1.44]), alongside the keyword counter's 87% / 0%.
Official guard-pipeline ASR after the edit: GaMS3 .982 EN / .972 SL; Gemma .738 EN / .103 SL.
GaMS3 band ranking at matched energy: B2 (layers 13-24) 0.50 / 0.30 residual Slovene strict refusal versus B1 0.97.
Utility cost and internal harm signal after abliteration (exp5): L28 harm signal halved in both languages; per-task utility table not given.

record.verdict_notes: This is an autonomous AI-generated research run; it is not peer reviewed. Slovene is machine-translated and Slovene judge agreement failed its kappa gate repeatedly (0.68-0.74). Only the README was read, and many numbers come from a hypothesis or plan document that mixes results with planned experiments. The tranche is changed to T3 (new cross-lingual setting with standard abliteration). Placement-contrast rows are relabelled as layer-dependence evidence (limits_scope for V2), not as plain support. Which party the GaMS3 edit was derived from is unclear; it appears each model had its own English-tuned Heretic run.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction activation ablation, addition, or general-capability test is reported.
The README reports selected weight-edit outcomes, not a systematic evaluation across released models or general capabilities.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or robustness training against its ablation is tested.
No comparison of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
The README compares refusal and actionability outcomes, but does not test how harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions are represented or encoded.
Reports language and checkpoint outcomes for English-derived edits; it does not test transfer from base to instruct models or across all language/model variants.
No manipulation or comparison of refusal-training regimes is reported.

tranche.reason: Applies Heretic abliteration, a difference-in-means weight edit, in a new setting (Slovene, the Gemma-3-12B / GaMS3 siblings, Qwen3-8B) and reports judged refusal before and after.

source_check.notes: The text is the repo README only (TL;DR, hypothesis block, artifact tables); paper.pdf is not included. The run is an autonomous AI-generated research pipeline: Slovene is machine-translated with native review pending, Slovene judge agreement missed its gate three times (kappa 0.68-0.74), and edits are NF4. The Gemma shipped edit's English refusal is unclear: the TL;DR judge gives 13% EN / 82% SL (model not named), while P-4 says the Gemma pick was judged 63/100.

statements.correction: Gemma, 8 groups matched on energy and layer count. Layers 16-31 leave EN 0.07 / SL 0.27. Layers 33-48 leave EN 0.92 / SL 0.92. A 2x dose of the late band leaves EN 0.88 / SL 0.92. Pooled high- minus low-overlap: EN -0.69 [-0.75, -0.62], SL -0.38 [-0.46, -0.31]. The label for this study is limits_scope.
statements.problem: Numbers right, but filed under 'challenges' with the framing 'edits confined to part of the network leave refusal intact'. Here both arms are partial-layer edits. The mid-band edit removes refusal and the late band does not. The record's verdict for this study is limits_scope (placement dependence), not challenges.

statements.correction: Gemma shipped edit: Slovene 94% -> 74%. GaMS3: Slovene 87% -> 0%. Each model's edit comes from its own English-objective Heretic search.
statements.problem: Facts right. Context omitted: the authors attribute the cross-language gap to an under-dosed, badly placed selected edit and say it is not a property of either model. Cited rows r5/r6 (broad 0.53 EN = 0.53 SL) show no language gap.
Consistent with the README. The reported edits are English-derived, and the Slovene refusal direction appears only as a cosine predictor.

statements.correction: Gemma, matched energy: layers 16-31 EN strict 0.07, layers 33-48 EN 0.92. Pooled EN -0.69 [-0.75, -0.62]. Qwen3-8B: 9/9 contrasts favour the better placement, 8/9 CIs exclude zero.
statements.problem: Right. Minor: the text gives one late band (layers 33-48) at 0.92, not several late-band edits.

statements.correction: Both values are Slovene. GaMS3 87% -> 0%, Gemma 94% -> 74%, each under its own English-objective Heretic edit. Under the best-placed Gemma edit, EN vs SL is strict 0.07 vs 0.27 and broad 0.53 vs 0.53.
statements.problem: Numbers right, but this study's contrast is between two checkpoints (GaMS3 vs Gemma) in the same evaluation language (Slovene). It is not an evaluation-language contrast. The authors attribute the Gemma result to the selected edit's dose and placement.

statements.correction: Gemma shipped edit: SL 94% -> 74%. Best-placed Gemma edit, EN vs SL: strict 0.07 vs 0.27, broad 0.53 vs 0.53, rubric ASR 0.93 vs 0.72. GaMS3: SL 87% -> 0%.
